---
description: Grill the reader before acting on an ambiguous or high-stakes request
---

You are running the grill-me interrogation.

Treat any text after this command as the request to grill. If there is none,
ask the reader for it first, then grill that request.

Apply the grill-me skill to the request:

1. Inspect the workspace first. Never ask what a file, a log or a command
   output can answer.
2. Ask exactly one question and stop. Give the context, the options and your
   recommendation, so the reader can answer in one word.
3. After each answer, either ask the next single question or play the
   decisions back as a numbered list with the plan that follows from them.
4. Cap the grill at five questions, then state the safest default and
   proceed unless the reader vetoes it.

Do not start the work until the reader confirms the play-back or says go.
